cand.title: 2027 Tax Education Forum in Punta Cana
cand.excerpt: Ranked on explicit dates and lodging/meeting mechanism, then reduced for named incumbent or unconfirmed accessibility.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Commercially relevant contacts, not verified hotel contract signatories: Carla Utter, NSTP Program Manager, is an operational routing candidate; Paul La Monaca, Vice President and Director of Education, develops live seminars and sets educational goals; Cameron Patterson is the published 2026 partner/vendor/sponsor contact. No source establishes any of them as the Punta Cana hotel buyer.
findings.futureEdition: Confirmed activity dates are May 4–6, 2027, not a publication date. Both the save-the-date and event product page identify Punta Cana; the product page lists 15 CPE credits. This edition falls inside the requested horizon. No subsequent Punta Cana edition through May 2028 was established.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: the beach-destination education and extracurricular concept is directionally suited to Wyndham Alltra Punta Cana’s guestroom-led all-inclusive resort product, rather than necessarily requiring a city convention hotel. Its approximately 300-person conference capacity and modest meeting footprint require validation against actual classroom layout, AV, breakouts and attendance. Resort-wide room count is not event demand. An all-inclusive package may simplify meals and companion stays, but budget acceptance and compulsory package terms are unknown.
findings.venueCommitments: No named 2027 host hotel or venue is published on the retrieved announcement or event product page. The announcement still says HOTEL DETAILS & BOOKING LINK TO BE RELEASED IN EARLY NOVEMBER and contains Hotel Name, WEBSITE HYPERLINK and XX/XX/2027 placeholders. A fresh retrieval did not resolve these placeholders. This does not establish that contracting is open, nor that no hotel has been selected privately.
findings.historicalRotation: Programme comparators, not proof of a single annual Punta Cana rotation: NSTP promoted Cabo San Lucas in May 2025 and Daytona Beach in October 2025; its July 21–23, 2026 Temecula Tax Education Forum used Temecula Creek Inn. In 2027 it announces Punta Cana May 4–6 and Nashville July 13–15, the latter at Hilton Garden Inn, Vanderbilt. These show multiple destination education events, not guaranteed annual return to Punta Cana.
findings.accommodationSourcing: The Punta Cana announcement anticipates a hotel reservation link and discounted-rate deadline, but both are placeholders; no actionable lodging link, cutoff, rate or room-block quantity was established. The 2026 Temecula comparator explicitly references contracted block dates and direct hotel booking/extension handling. Inference: an organizer-coordinated host-hotel booking pathway is plausible for Punta Cana, but its terms, buyer and procurement stage remain unverified. No PCO, DMC or housing agency was identified in the reviewed event materials.
findings.organizationStructure: NSTP is the National Society of Tax Professionals, a nonprofit founded in 1985 serving tax professionals through education and professional support. It is the organizer/promoter of this programme, not evidenced as a travel agency, PCO or DMC. The supplied travel-trade-intermediary segment should not be treated as verified organizational classification.
findings.competitiveLimitations: No named incumbent for Punta Cana, overflow requirement, sold-out block, attendance or room-demand figure was established. Temecula Creek Inn is a historical comparator, and the Nashville Hilton Garden Inn is a different 2027 event, not the Punta Cana incumbent. Do not infer either accessible overflow or commitment to a competing Punta Cana hotel.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Recommendation: contact NSTP through its published taxes@nstp.org or 800-367-8130 channel, asking for Carla Utter and the person responsible for Punta Cana lodging/meetings; involve Paul La Monaca for programme requirements. First establish whether May 4–6, 2027 has a signed host agreement and who controls procurement. If genuinely open, request arrival/departure pattern, peak rooms, classroom attendance, breakouts, AV and all-inclusive budget before offering a tailored resort proposal. If committed, avoid speculative overflow selling; ask permission to enter the next destination-programme review and establish its decision timetable. Cameron Patterson is a separate sponsorship relationship route, not a presumed hotel buyer.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: For the selected May 2027 edition, accessibility is unknown: dates and destination are confirmed, but an unpublished hotel name is not evidence of open sourcing. Treat as a qualification conversation, not an RFP, available room block, or displacement opportunity. There is no sourced basis to say demand is already committed to another hotel, and equally no basis to say it remains contestable.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: the multi-destination educational programme supports cultivating a future resort-host relationship even if 2027 is already contracted. A future Punta Cana return, 2028 date, sourcing cycle and competitive bid have not been verified. Do not label this an annually recurring Punta Cana opportunity or count Nashville as Dominican Republic demand.
